ABB.rationale: July was strong (record Q2 CY26 orders +50%, ₹90 special dividend) but margins are tightening, consensus is Hold with targets below spot, and valuation downgrades persist.
ABB.watch: Two straight quarters of margin recovery justifies a re-rating; cost/competition pressure keeps it capped.

ABB.rationale: Management's supply-strain comment for 2027-28 is the most bullish forward statement any company in this basket has made, and Electrification orders +77% on data centres backs it. But margins are compressing on copper, the headline P/E is flattered by Rs1,799 cr of other income, and 107x leaves nothing for the cycle turning.
ABB.watch: Margin recovery as copper pass-through catches up, or a de-rating that reflects the other-income distortion.

ADANIGREEN.rationale: Despite a Q1 profit rise, the stock hit a two-month low as Bernstein flagged the merchant-portfolio + BESS transfer to AESL (structural loss of upside) plus curtailment EBITDA hits; at ~140x+ the overhang likely dominates the quarter.
ADANIGREEN.watch: Favorable transfer terms for AGEL shareholders or curtailment easing neutralizes the bear case.

ADANIGREEN.rationale: At 114x with 20 GW operational, the equity is priced on FY31 capacity that depends on transmission the government's own planning has not built. The value being moved to Adani Energy Solutions is the specific problem: you hold the capex and someone else holds the merchant upside. Curtailment is already showing in the numbers, and no disclosed data-centre PPA exists.
ADANIGREEN.watch: A named data-centre PPA, or the merchant/BESS transfer being priced transparently.

ADANIGREEN.rationale: Analyst targets span Rs1,000 to Rs1,800 - a 1.8x spread that tells you the valuation is unanchored. The specific issues are dated and real: grid curtailment already cost 5-7% of Q1 EBITDA, transmission delays are being modelled by the bulls as a base case, and the merchant and BESS portfolios are being moved to a sibling entity.
ADANIGREEN.watch: Curtailment normalising in H2 FY27 as guided would remove the largest identified drag.

ANANTRAJ.rationale: Fell ~30% from its 2026 peak and is rebuilding; the July demerger approval is a positive but value unlock is slow (NCLT) and DC revenue is still tiny vs the ₹1,200 cr FY27 ambition, capping near-term re-rating.
ANANTRAJ.watch: Large hyperscaler tenancy contract or faster demerger timeline flips this to up.

ANANTRAJ.rationale: Demerger is progressing and the MW roadmap is now explicit, but FY27 adds only 35 MW and DC revenue stays small against a realty P&L. At 38x with the value-unlock gated on NCLT timing, the re-rating needs a tenant contract, not a scheme filing.
ANANTRAJ.watch: A named hyperscaler tenancy at Manesar or Andhra, or NCLT approval landing inside FY27.

APARINDS.rationale: Fresh large beat (Q1 FY27 PAT +78%, stock +9% on results) with Buy consensus and conductor/cable export demand from US grid + DC buildout; already doubled in six months so gains should be choppier from here.
APARINDS.watch: Adverse US tariff news or an export slowdown is what breaks the uptrend.

APARINDS.rationale: Q1 was genuinely strong with profit up 78% and management naming data-centre demand. But you are being asked to buy after a 17% move driven by a dilutive raise whose purpose has not been disclosed, at 57x, with the share count about to increase. Wait for the use of proceeds.
APARINDS.watch: QIP proceeds earmarked for conductor or cable capacity serving data centres.

APARINDS.rationale: Up 17% since the 2 August call, and the identifiable driver is the QIP announced 10 August rather than any operating news - results were 24 July. A Rs2,500 cr primary raise at a 10% discount is dilution with an undisclosed purpose, which is not usually what a stock rallies on. The next three months are about what the money is for.
APARINDS.watch: Disclosure of the QIP use of proceeds - capacity expansion would read very differently from debt reduction.

ARE&M.rationale: Deeply out of favor (near 52-week lows, ~19x — a big peer discount) with lead-acid margins pressured and lithium pushed to FY27; the 60 MWh qualification plant commissioning is real but momentum needs an earnings or gigafactory trigger.
ARE&M.watch: First marquee cell-qualification customer or a margin beat starts a re-rating; further lithium delays keep it a value trap.

ARE&M.rationale: Cheap at 24x with the new-energy pivot showing genuine operating leverage for the first time - losses narrowing on 72% growth is the number that matters. But the data-centre link is indirect: BESS serves grid and commercial storage, and the connection to AI infrastructure is inference rather than disclosure. Lithium is still 5% of the company against a Rs95bn capex commitment.
ARE&M.watch: A BESS order specifically for data-centre backup, or lithium reaching 10% of revenue.

ARE&M.rationale: The new-energy segment is finally scaling with losses narrowing rather than widening - Rs22 cr from Rs35 cr on 72% revenue growth - and the 10 GWh BESS facility is targeted operational in Q3 FY27. The market took the print up 8%. Margin compression in the core lead-acid business is the offset.
ARE&M.watch: New-energy losses widening again would remove the reason to own it.

BBOX.rationale: Choppy in 2026 with a ~58x trailing P/E resting on margin expansion while topline growth stays muted; the AI-DC networking narrative needs visible large deal wins to sustain the multiple.
BBOX.watch: A marquee AI-DC order flips it up; another flat-revenue quarter at 58x pressures it down.

BBOX.rationale: Backlog nearly doubled and the company now has a named Tier-1 hyperscaler relationship it did not have a quarter ago. At 52x that is not cheap, but the multiple is against a backlog with 65-75% visible growth guided, and the stock sits 23% below its 52-week high. The risk is concentration: this is a levered bet on US data-centre construction with no India buffer.
BBOX.watch: US hyperscaler capex guidance turning down, or backlog conversion slipping two consecutive quarters.

BBOX.rationale: The 12-13 Aug print is the strongest evidence in the whole theme: backlog +83% to an all-time high, a first-time Tier-1 hyperscaler win at $131mn, and explicit FY27 booking guidance. Execution is the only question left, not demand.
BBOX.watch: A US hyperscaler capex pause would hit this harder than any India-facing name.

BHARTIARTL.rationale: Steady ARPU-led compounding; Q1 FY27 (Aug 4) expected to show continued ARPU/5G momentum, and the market is positioning for the next tariff hike in H2 2026. Near highs but valuation is earnings-supported, not narrative.
BHARTIARTL.watch: Tariff-hike delay past 2026 or a soft ARPU print shifts it to sideways.

BHARTIARTL.rationale: The Nxtra 1 GW ambition is funded, the land vehicles are being bought, and the core telecom business is deleveraging fast with ARPU still rising. Buy the compounding and treat the DC arm as free optionality - but be honest that at Rs12 lakh cr market cap the DC piece cannot move the P&L for years. This is not a clean expression of the AI-infra trade.
BHARTIARTL.watch: Nxtra being carved out or separately funded at a disclosed valuation.

BLUESTARCO.rationale: Corrected and basing near the lower end of its range while the AC cycle turns up (strong summer sell-through, ~15% FY27 AC growth guidance); Aug 7 results plus festive restocking give favorable risk-reward from a washed-out base.
BLUESTARCO.watch: A weak Q1 or renewed channel-inventory glut negates the recovery thesis.

BLUESTARCO.rationale: Genuinely the best-quantified data-centre revenue path of any name here: Rs1,500 cr booked in one quarter, a Rs3,000 cr FY27 target, and 20% of revenue guided by FY29 at better margins and payment terms. The problem is that two-thirds of the company is a room-AC business whose margins just halved, and at 58x on already-depressed earnings you are paying a full price to own that cycle while you wait for the DC piece.
BLUESTARCO.watch: RAC margin stabilising, or the DC segment being reported separately so it can be valued on its own.

BLUESTARCO.rationale: Two businesses moving in opposite directions. Room AC margins halved on commodity inflation, a short summer and dealer inventory - that is what took the stock down 12%. Meanwhile the data-centre MEP business booked Rs1,500 cr in a single quarter against a Rs3,000 cr full-year target. Over three months the RAC cycle dominates; the DC story is a FY29 argument.
BLUESTARCO.watch: RAC margin recovering toward the guided 6.5% EBIT would flip this back to up.

CGPOWER.rationale: Strong Q1 FY27 (PAT +27%, order book +45%) and near highs, but ~90-120x P/E plus the unresolved ₹900 cr Tallgrass/Crusoe US DC order overhang cap near-term upside; execution is priced in.
CGPOWER.watch: Tallgrass contract confirmed (or replaced) flips to up; cancellation triggers a de-rate.

CGPOWER.rationale: Order book +45% and the US data-centre transformer order (Rs900 cr, January) is real, but at 109x earnings and 17x book the multiple demands flawless execution across transformers, switchgear and a new semiconductor venture simultaneously. The only dated broker target on file sits below the current price.
CGPOWER.watch: Another US data-centre export order of comparable size, or CG Semi revenue being disclosed separately.

CUMMINSIND.rationale: Clear multi-quarter demand runway from DC gensets and CPCB4+ price/mix gains, with the stock ~10% off its high into Aug 6 results — a fundamentals-led uptrend at a demanding but not extreme ~65x.
CUMMINSIND.watch: Powergen guidance below ~20% or export weakness stalls the move.

CUMMINSIND.rationale: If you want proof the India data-centre capex cycle is real and being delivered, this is the disclosure that proves it - 40% of powergen revenue, with customers pulling delivery forward. The reason it is not a buy is arithmetic: PAT was flat YoY, management has guided margins will not recover quickly, and it trades at 61x with the MD departing. Excellent demand already fully paid for.
CUMMINSIND.watch: Gross margin recovery showing up in Q2, or a credible MD successor being named.

CUMMINSIND.rationale: The demand disclosure is the strongest anywhere in this basket - 40% of powergen revenue is data centres and customers want gensets sooner, not later. But profit was flat year-on-year because margins have not recovered, management explicitly guided that they will not recover quickly, and the MD leaves at the end of this month. Demand is not the constraint; conversion to profit is.
CUMMINSIND.watch: Gross margin moving back toward 36% would make this an up call immediately.

DIXON.rationale: Already ~35% off its high and Q1 FY27 confirmed decelerating growth with margin contraction as mobiles-PLI hypergrowth normalizes; much of the correction is done but no near-term catalyst reverses the narrative before Q2.
DIXON.watch: Restored volume guidance or a large anchor win flips it up; another guidance cut breaks support.

DIXON.rationale: Belongs in this theme only as a partial-exposure name and Q1 argues it belongs on the wrong side of it. A 3% EBITDA margin business at 46x, with the headline profit flattered by a one-off and management deferring recovery to FY28, is not where the AI capex cycle pays you.
DIXON.watch: A disclosed data-centre or server-assembly revenue line, or EBITDA margin back above 3.5%.

E2E.rationale: Q1 FY27 revenue +334% with PAT swinging to ₹44 cr on B200 cluster deployment — the L&T-backed AI-cloud ramp is now visibly profitable. High beta and capex funding needs cap conviction at medium.
E2E.watch: A dilutive fundraise or QoQ revenue stall breaks the momentum trade.

E2E.rationale: This is a valuation call, not a business call. Revenue growth is genuine and the margin is extraordinary, but trailing ROCE is still negative, the TTM profit base is about Rs31 cr, and the shares are up 208% in a year. At 400x-plus any multiple is arithmetic noise; you are underwriting FY29 with no disclosed capex plan to check it against.
E2E.watch: A disclosed multi-year capex and contracted-revenue plan that makes the forward multiple computable.

E2E.rationale: The business is inflecting hard - revenue up 334% at 75% EBITDA margin - but nothing has been added to the story since 22 July, and the shares are up 110% in three months and 208% in a year. The next three months are about whether Q2 confirms the run-rate, with no catalyst scheduled in between.
E2E.watch: A disclosed capex plan or a large sovereign/enterprise GPU contract.

ENRIN.rationale: Consolidating ~10-15% below its post-listing high; consensus Hold with average target near spot (~96x P/E), though last quarter's ~80% profit jump keeps downside limited.
ENRIN.watch: A large HVDC order or big quarterly beat pushes it out of the range upward.

ENRIN.rationale: Operationally the best margin story in the group - 430bps of expansion with PAT up 68% - and the returns on capital are genuinely exceptional. But it has disclosed no data-centre order at all, did not publish quarterly order inflow, and trades at 83x and 26x book. The AI-infra attribution here is inference from the grid-transition narrative, not from anything the company has said.
ENRIN.watch: A disclosed data-centre or grid-for-DC order, or order inflow being published.

FINCABLES.rationale: The laggard of the cable pack — recent profit pressure, missed the sector's 2026 re-rating, upgraded late July purely on 'improved valuation'. Cheap but with no growth catalyst or momentum: a value wait, not a directional trade.
FINCABLES.watch: Volume re-acceleration or promoter-overhang resolution starts a catch-up trade.

FINCABLES.rationale: Genuinely the cheapest well-run name here at 27x with a 59% profit beat, and the fibre expansion is real. The problem is category: management attributes growth to agriculture, industrial and solar, and has never mentioned data centres. It is a good business at a fair price that does not belong in an AI-infra basket - which is why the grade is hold rather than buy on this thesis.
FINCABLES.watch: A disclosed data-centre or hyperscaler fibre order would move this to buy on the theme.

FINCABLES.rationale: A 59% profit beat took it to a 52-week high and it is up 25% since the 2 August call. The fibre capacity coming on stream in Q3 FY27 is the near-term driver. But note what management actually credited: agriculture, industrial and solar - not data centres.
FINCABLES.watch: Copper rod plant restarting would add back a line that went to near-zero.

HFCL.rationale: Q1 FY27 swung from loss to ~₹245 cr profit and July brought ~₹940 cr of DC-fibre export orders, validating the OptiQ AI-DC pivot; order momentum plus turnaround supports a positive lean, execution history warrants caution.
HFCL.watch: If Q2 shows Q1 profit was provision-reversal-driven, the rally unwinds.

HFCL.rationale: Order book is real and large, but conversion is the disclosed bottleneck and the Rs400 cr capex to fix it only lands in FY28. The stock is up 220% in a year at its 52-week high, and I could not resolve the P/E to better than a 59-105x range. The buyer of the $1.10bn contract has never been named as a hyperscaler in a filing - that characterisation comes from secondary sources only.
HFCL.watch: Identifying the March contract counterparty, or order conversion visibly accelerating.

HFCL.rationale: Incremental news since 31 July is ~Rs523 cr of export orders against an Rs21,200 cr book, plus a capex approval and a US policy headline that is still speculative. Everything structural - the $1.10bn five-year contract and the Q1 swing to profit - was already in the price before August. Screener flags capacity constraints impacting order conversion, which is exactly what the Rs400 cr capex addresses but not before FY28.
HFCL.watch: Conversion improving would re-rate it; the March contract counterparty has still never been identified as a hyperscaler in any filing.

ITI.rationale: Consensus expects another Q1 FY27 loss on declining revenue; the big Q4 FY26 profit looks one-off and moves are speculative circuit-driven spikes. Loss-making PSU at a speculative valuation with no confirmed catalyst leans negative.
ITI.watch: A major BharatNet allocation or revival package triggers a circuit-driven rally and voids the down call.

ITI.rationale: ROE of -9.1% and ROCE of 1.4% at 14.9x book, with a trailing profit figure so distorted by a one-off that no source agrees on a P/E. The Airtel MoU is a positive but carries no disclosed value, and the credit rating is still sub-investment grade at BB+. There is no data-centre revenue here at all.
ITI.watch: Q1 FY27 results showing sustainable operating profit, or the Airtel MoU being quantified.

KAYNES.rationale: Recovering off its 2026 correction low with strong structural news (OSAT ramp, ISM 2.0 JV plans, 30% FY27 growth guidance); very rich valuation makes the up-lean low-conviction and results-dependent.
KAYNES.watch: A Q1 margin miss at ~100x earnings triggers a sharp de-rate.

KAYNES.rationale: Classified in this theme as an AI beneficiary, but its own Q1 deck says the opposite - AI demand is raising its input costs. At 73x with profit falling and the OSAT payoff deferred to Q3 FY27, the multiple is paying for a semiconductor story that has not started. The 50% de-rating already reflects most of this, which is why it is not a sell.
KAYNES.watch: OSAT revenue landing on time in Q3 FY27 with margins holding above 15%.

KAYNES.rationale: Q1 inverted the thesis: revenue grew 40% but profit fell 24%, because AI data-centre demand is bidding away the memory and wafer capacity Kaynes buys. The stock has already de-rated 50% from its high, so the damage is done, but OSAT revenue is deferred to Q3 FY27 and there is no margin catalyst before then.
KAYNES.watch: Component costs normalising, or ISM 2.0 JV applications being accepted.

KEI.rationale: Surged into its Q1 FY27 results (board Aug 3) with management targeting 20% growth as Sanand capacity ramps into the power/DC capex surge — momentum, capacity and demand aligned near term.
KEI.watch: A growth/margin miss vs the guided 20%, or a copper shock, stalls the run.

KEI.rationale: The most credible DC quantification in the cables group is still the chairman's February comment about capturing Rs2,500-3,000 cr of a ~Rs25,000 cr multi-year opportunity - an opportunity, not revenue. Q1 exports actually fell 7.3%. At 55x with a Hold initiation from CLSA and nothing new in six weeks, the AI premium is doing the work.
KEI.watch: EHV or DC cable disclosed as a revenue segment with a growth rate attached.

KIRLOSENG.rationale: Nearly doubled in a year on the genset/DC theme and now trades close to consensus targets at ~47x with valuation downgrades appearing; the ₹1,400 cr expansion is long-dated — expect digestion rather than another leg up.
KIRLOSENG.watch: A Q1 beat with raised guidance extends the rally; in-line means consolidation after the ~98% run.

KIRLOSENG.rationale: The 192 MW HyperNext order is real evidence and the O&M tail is valuable, but the quarter showed the cost of getting there - margins down 230bps, profit down 17%, exports down 11%. At 53x you are paying a growth multiple for a business whose profits fell. Cheaper and better-disclosed exposure to the same genset demand exists at Cummins.
KIRLOSENG.watch: Margin recovery plus a disclosed data-centre revenue share.

LT.rationale: Best risk-reward large-cap in the theme: Q1 FY27 PAT +14% with a record ₹7.79 lakh cr order book (+27%), reasonable ~33x valuation, and Middle East / offshore-wind / DC order momentum continuing into H2.
LT.watch: Core E&C margin disappointment or an oil-driven Middle East capex slowdown stalls the uptrend.

LT.rationale: At 31x with a Rs7.78 lakh cr order book, this is the one way to hold the AI-infra build where a disappointment does not break the thesis - hydrocarbon, infrastructure and defence carry it regardless. The Together AI award adds a genuine, named, gigawatt-scale AI franchise on top, at a multiple less than a quarter of what the pure-plays cost. Diversification is the whole argument.
LT.watch: AI Factory execution slipping, or the Together AI counterparty running into funding trouble.

LT.rationale: Three large orders inside two weeks, one of them the single biggest AI-infrastructure contract awarded to an Indian company. The Together AI order converts L&T from an EPC contractor near the theme into a named principal in it, and the Chennai site is designed for gigawatt expansion beyond phase 1.
LT.watch: Together AI is a single counterparty for a very large order - counterparty funding is the risk to watch.

MARINE.rationale: Steady drip of defence/DC power-distribution orders keeps the story alive, but it is a thin small-cap at ~60x P/E consolidating below its high with no single large near-term catalyst.
MARINE.watch: A single ₹300 cr+ DC or navy order breaks it to new highs; an order lull leaves it drifting.

MARINE.rationale: The clearest case in the basket of price arriving without evidence. Up 29% in eleven days and 124% in a year, at roughly 85-90x, on a micro-cap that has not reported the June quarter and has formally told the exchange there is nothing to disclose. The Princeton Digital order is real and encouraging at Rs142 cr - but it is one order, pre-dates the move, and does not support the multiple.
MARINE.watch: Q1 FY27 results showing the DC order converting, plus a second named customer.

MARINE.rationale: Up 29% in eleven days with no results, no order announcement, and the company itself telling the exchange on 10 August that nothing is pending. The only identifiable driver is a Rs141.74 cr order from 28 July that was already public. A micro-cap at ~85x with an unexplained move and an exchange query on file is a poor risk-reward into results it has not yet scheduled.
MARINE.watch: A results date being announced, or a second named data-centre order.

NETWEB.rationale: Blowout Q1 FY27 (PAT +180%, order book ₹2,507 cr) with broker buys, while the stock has already corrected ~20% from its June high — froth partly worked off with fundamentals accelerating. Risk: ~66x forward P/E and working capital.
NETWEB.watch: GPU supply constraints or an order-book stall invalidates the case at 66x forward.

NETWEB.rationale: The cleanest listed AI-compute pure-play in India and the delivery is real - AI systems are 62% of revenue, up nearly 5x. But at 113x and 41x book, sitting at its 52-week high after +144% in a year, the price already assumes the pipeline converts. Nothing new since 29 July to extend the story.
NETWEB.watch: Pipeline conversion running below the guided 60%, or a large IndiaAI order landing.

POLYCAB.rationale: Strong Q1 FY27 (revenue +39%) with brokerages retaining Buys (targets ₹10,160-11,100), but the stock sold off on results after a 21% one-month run at 42x FY27E — fundamentals argue up, extended positioning argues consolidation first.
POLYCAB.watch: A copper spike or Q2 margin miss at 42x converts this to a valuation de-rate.

POLYCAB.rationale: Q1 was strong (revenue +39%, PAT +33%) but reported before this window and driven by housing and infra wiring, not data centres. Management has never quantified a DC revenue share. Sector work implies wires and cables capture only a low-single-digit share of DC capex spread across the whole industry, so at 49x you are paying a premium multiple for a thematic label the company has not claimed.
POLYCAB.watch: Management quantifying data-centre revenue as a disclosed segment.

POWERGRID.rationale: The sector laggard (~18x, ~3% yield, near oversold) with a defensive regulated model; accelerating transmission capex should eventually lift capitalization but no near-term catalyst is big enough to break the range in three months.
POWERGRID.watch: A step-up in quarterly capitalization starts a re-rating; tariff-review noise is the downside.

POWERGRID.rationale: Power is the binding constraint on India's data-centre build - facilities take 12-18 months, the grid takes 3-5 years - and the government just doubled its own AI load estimate to 26.3 GW by FY32. Power Grid is the monopoly builder of that grid, guiding Rs37,000 cr of FY27 capex with Rs1.75 lakh cr of work in hand, and it trades at 15.8x with a 3.3% yield after falling on a timing-driven quarter. The cheapest name here with the most direct claim on the constraint everyone else is competing around.
POWERGRID.watch: Capitalisation slipping below the Rs30,000 cr guide, or regulated ROE being cut in the next tariff period.

POWERGRID.rationale: Fell 7% since the 2 August call on a Q1 miss that was regulatory timing, not demand - while the government simultaneously doubled its own estimate of AI data-centre load to 26.3 GW by FY32. Capitalisation tripled YoY and FY27 guidance is Rs37,000 cr of capex. The setup is a de-rated price against an upgraded structural driver.
POWERGRID.watch: Further regulatory or tariff-order adverse timing would push the recovery out another quarter.

POWERINDIA.rationale: Strongest earnings-beat streak in the T&D pack with the HVDC/grid pipeline still building and Q1 FY27 (Aug 7) a live catalyst — but at ~150x+ trailing P/E any miss gets punished hard.
POWERINDIA.watch: A Q1 margin/revenue miss at this valuation turns the call down quickly.

POWERINDIA.rationale: Best-evidenced name in the power layer and the operational delivery is outstanding. The grade is entirely a price problem: 134x earnings and 31x book means the Karjan capacity completing in December 2028 is already in the stock. You are buying excellent execution at a multiple that requires it to continue uninterrupted for four years.
POWERINDIA.watch: A de-rating toward 90x on unchanged fundamentals, or the Barmer HVDC award landing.

POWERINDIA.rationale: The clearest DC order disclosure of any power-equipment name - specific MVA figures, not commentary - alongside record backlog and margin expansion of 450bps. The customer mix shifting out of utilities into industry is the AI-infra transition showing up in the order book itself.
POWERINDIA.watch: Transmission-order timing slippage, which management already flagged for H1 FY27.

RAILTEL.rationale: Q1 FY27 grew ~20% but profit slipped on a low-margin project mix and the stock fell on results; steady small orders support the floor but are too small to re-rate a cooled PSU-telecom trade.
RAILTEL.watch: A ₹500 cr+ Kavach/DC order or clear margin recovery turns it up; another margin miss turns it down.

RAILTEL.rationale: Order book and intake are genuinely strong and the DC number is disclosed rather than aspirational, but PAT went nowhere because receivables are deteriorating - debtors at 175 days with ECL provisions now hitting the P&L. A PSU collecting slowly from government customers is a working-capital story before it is an AI story.
RAILTEL.watch: Debtor days falling below 140, or the Noida 10 MW commissioning pulling forward.

RRKABEL.rationale: Spectacular Q1 FY27 (PAT +129%) but the stock is parabolic — +112% in three months to new highs, with analysts themselves flagging valuation; growth is real but fully priced for the next quarter. Risk/reward favors consolidation.
RRKABEL.watch: A shallow pullback holding support with Q2 growth intact turns it up; growth normalization triggers sharp mean-reversion.

RRKABEL.rationale: Up 46% in three months and 135% in a year with no disclosed data-centre revenue, no order announcement and no news at all in six weeks. At 52x earnings and roughly 37x EV/EBITDA this is a housing and consumer-wiring business carrying an AI-infra multiple. Held rather than sold only because there is no company-specific negative to point at.
RRKABEL.watch: Any disclosed data-centre or EHV order, or the multiple compressing toward the sector.

SCHNEIDER.rationale: Up ~110% in a year to ~120x P/E while FY26 profit actually fell ~21% — a fragile combination; the DC/T&D narrative supports the price but earnings must catch up. Choppy consolidation with downside risk on any weak print.
SCHNEIDER.watch: A strong profit rebound validates the multiple; another decline likely triggers a sharp correction.

SCHNEIDER.rationale: The most expensive name in the theme at 148x earnings and 43x book, on trailing profits that FELL 21% in FY26 with a Q4 down 60%. It has disclosed no data-centre order, no export order and no capacity expansion, and it has not yet reported the June quarter. A 148x multiple on declining earnings with no evidence attached is the clearest risk-reward mismatch in the list.
SCHNEIDER.watch: The 17 August Q1 print showing a genuine earnings inflection with DC orders named.

STLTECH.rationale: Record Q1 FY27 (highest-ever revenue/EBITDA/order book, +87% on AI-DC fibre demand) with FY27 margin guidance raised to 23% and the chart near a multi-year breakout — turnaround plus rising guidance into Q2.
STLTECH.watch: US tariff escalation, hyperscaler order pullback, or leverage news stalls the turnaround.

STLTECH.rationale: This is a valuation hold, not a scepticism hold. The $1.11bn hyperscaler award and an Rs18,618 cr order book against Rs4,745 cr of FY26 revenue is a genuine inflection. But at 142x and 14x book, the price already discounts FY27-FY29 delivery, and on 8 June 2026 this stock hit a 5% lower circuit on a single Broadcom guidance headline. High beta to US AI sentiment with no domestic buffer.
STLTECH.watch: Two quarters of delivery at the guided 23% margin would justify buying it; a US AI-capex scare would take it down 30% first.

STLTECH.rationale: The August orders add ~Rs2,800 cr to an Rs18,618 cr book that was already disclosed in the 24 July results - real but incremental. The move since has been driven by a US trade action that is still only a draft FCC rule. With the stock at its 52-week high after +390% in a year, the next three months hinge on whether that rule is finalised, not on India demand.
STLTECH.watch: The FCC proposal being finalised would extend this; being dropped would remove the August catalyst entirely.

TARIL.rationale: Momentum clearly negative (-30% over a year) and Q1 FY27 missed again (PAT -9%) on Changodar capacity constraints; estimates being cut despite a record order book.
TARIL.watch: Revenue re-acceleration as new capacity ships ends the de-rating; until then rallies get sold.

TARIL.rationale: The cheapest transformer name after the 45% drawdown, with a record Rs6,630 cr order book that has not yet reached the revenue line - 8% growth against a book that size is the disconnect to watch. No DC order has ever been named. This is a recovery candidate rather than an AI-infra holding.
TARIL.watch: Revenue growth accelerating into double digits as the order book converts.

TARIL.rationale: Already down 45% from its 52-week high, which is most of a de-rating from a much richer multiple. The order book is at a record but revenue grew only 8% and there has been no news for six weeks. At 34x the fall has done its work; there is no visible catalyst either way over three months.
TARIL.watch: Order-book conversion showing up in revenue, or a data-centre transformer order being named.

TATACOMM.rationale: Q1 FY27 missed estimates even with digital growing ~17%; brokerages kept Buys only with trimmed targets — the AI/data-platform re-rating needs digital-margin proof. Range-bound until Q2 shows inflection.
TATACOMM.watch: Digital EBITDA margin turning up, or a large sovereign-AI contract, moves this to up.

TATACOMM.rationale: Sold ~74% of its data-centre business to STT GDC and retains 26% - this is a connectivity play, not a DC landlord, and the theme label overstates it. Profit fell 44% last quarter, the multiple is 48x, and nothing has been added since. The Rs8,400 cr DC-interconnect opportunity management cites is a target, not revenue.
TATACOMM.watch: DC-interconnect revenue being disclosed as a separate line, or the contingent-liability overhang resolving.

TATAPOWER.rationale: Q1 FY27 beat (PAT +11%) yet the stock slipped — range-bound for a year at ~35x; Citi's bullish call argues eventual upside but near-term triggers before November are modest.
TATAPOWER.watch: A breakout on a large transmission/DC-power win confirms the bull case; weak monsoon power demand keeps the range.

TATAPOWER.rationale: Reasonably priced at 31x for a diversified utility with a genuine renewables and transmission pipeline, and it would benefit from data-centre load in aggregate. But it has signed no disclosed data-centre PPA, and the theme attribution is generic - any Indian generator benefits if 26 GW of DC load arrives. Held as a utility, not as an AI-infra expression.
TATAPOWER.watch: A named data-centre or hyperscaler power purchase agreement.

TDPOWERSYS.rationale: Strongest momentum in the group (+~178% 1-yr, repeated highs) with genuine DC/gas-turbine generator demand and a record order book; trend and order flow favor continuation, but ~85x P/E after a parabolic run is pullback-prone.
TDPOWERSYS.watch: Any slowdown in US DC genset ordering triggers sharp mean-reversion given the run-up.

TDPOWERSYS.rationale: The evidence is close to best-in-class - named repeat orders from global OEMs for US data-centre gensets, 87% inflow growth, guidance raised. The grade is a timing call: 84x after +33% in eleven days and +192% in a year, with domestic orders deliberately shrunk to Rs50 cr. Everything now depends on US data-centre construction with essentially no India buffer.
TDPOWERSYS.watch: A second quarter at similar inflow would justify paying up; any US hyperscaler capex wobble hits this first.

TDPOWERSYS.rationale: Outstanding quarter and a guidance raise - but the stock has already taken it, up 33% in eleven days. Note the qualifier the market glossed over: domestic inflow collapsed to Rs50 cr as the company deliberately prioritised export margin. That makes the whole story a bet on US data-centre demand, and the news is now out.
TDPOWERSYS.watch: Repeat orders from the same global OEMs would confirm the run-rate; a US capex pause removes 93% of the inflow.

TECHNOE.rationale: Consolidating rather than overheated while the core T&D EPC cycle stays strong and the 36 MW AI-ready Chennai DC is now live and monetizable; reasonable valuation vs AI-infra peers gives room if DC customer wins land.
TECHNOE.watch: No DC tenant announcement by Q2 results fades the AI angle to a sideways EPC story.

TECHNOE.rationale: Cheapest of the DC names at 26x and 36% below its 52-week high, with an order book beating target and near-zero debt. But management has just told you the DC monetisation is years out, and working capital at 430 days is the real constraint. Cheap for a reason that is now disclosed rather than hidden.
TECHNOE.watch: DC revenue guidance for FY28 above Rs300 cr, or working-capital days below 350.

TECHNOE.rationale: The 12 Aug call reset the DC timeline: Rs1,000 cr of capex against Rs40-50 cr of FY27 DC revenue, and the market marked it down 7%. Core EPC and smart metering are delivering and order inflow beat the annual target, so the floor is solid, but the DC re-rating is a FY29 story on these numbers.
TECHNOE.watch: A signed colocation contract at Chennai, or DC revenue guidance moving up from Rs40-50 cr.

TEJASNET.rationale: Q1 FY27 net loss widened to ~₹202 cr even as revenue doubled off a weak base; near 52-week lows after the BSNL 4G order tapered with no comparable follow-on in hand — momentum, earnings and order visibility all negative into Q2.
TEJASNET.watch: A large BSNL follow-on or export order sharply reverses the down call.

TEJASNET.rationale: Loss-making at the operating level with Rs4,277 cr of net debt against an Rs1,529 cr order book, and no data-centre revenue disclosed. BSNL and BharatNet order flow - the actual driver of this business - produced nothing in the window. A levered, loss-making equipment maker is the wrong vehicle for a capex theme regardless of how strong the theme is.
TEJASNET.watch: A return to operating profit, or a BharatNet award large enough to cover the debt service.

VINDHYATEL.rationale: Thinly covered holdco/cables-EPC proxy with no company-specific news flow and no identifiable Aug-Oct catalyst beyond BharatNet III EPC hopes; trades on holdco-discount math, not the AI narrative.
VINDHYATEL.watch: A sizeable BharatNet/utility EPC win or holdco-discount narrowing sparks a re-rate.

VINDHYATEL.rationale: Optically the cheapest name in the theme at 13x and below book, and the cable division genuinely doubled EBITDA. But the P/E is flattered by Rs257 cr of other income, EPC is shrinking on government payment delays, and receivables are Rs733 cr against a Rs3,056 cr market cap. No data-centre or hyperscaler order at all - the AI-infra link here is indirect.
VINDHYATEL.watch: EPC revenue recovering as government funds release, or receivables falling materially.

VOLTAMP.rationale: Solid Q1 FY27 (revenue +28%, PAT +15%) but margin erosion is flagged and the stock is still ~25% below its high after the Q4 FY26 crash — a basing stock, not a momentum one.
VOLTAMP.watch: Margin stabilization for a second quarter re-rates it; renewed slippage revisits the lows.

VOLTAMP.rationale: Cheapest credible way into the transformer layer at 32x, net cash, and the only company here putting its own money specifically into the dry-type format data centres use. It sits 19% below its 52-week high while the rest of the power group is at or near highs. The risk is real: margins compressed hard in Q1 and there is no order book to check the trajectory against.
VOLTAMP.watch: A second quarter of raw-material-driven margin compression would take this back to hold.

VOLTAMP.rationale: The Rs90 cr dry-type transformer plant is a direct, self-funded bet on the format data centres actually buy, and it is sized for demand over five to six years. Revenue grew 28% and the company is net cash. The offset is margin: input costs rose 42% against 28% revenue growth, and Voltamp does not disclose an order book, so there is no visibility between quarters.
VOLTAMP.watch: Voltamp discloses no order book, so a quarterly miss arrives without warning.

VOLTAS.rationale: Record 1-million-unit AC quarter confirms demand recovery while the stock trades near the bottom of its 52-week range on depressed FY26 earnings — a strong Q1 print can drive mean-reversion, though price competition keeps margin risk alive.
VOLTAS.watch: If record volumes don't translate into margin/PAT recovery, it stays stuck near lows.

VOLTAS.rationale: Carries no disclosed data-centre revenue at all, so its presence in this basket is thematic association rather than evidence. It trades at 108x on trough earnings with ROE at 6.1%, and it reports tomorrow into exactly the conditions that just produced a 15% profit decline and a 12% share fall at its closest comparable. Nothing here is an AI-infrastructure holding.
VOLTAS.watch: A disclosed data-centre cooling order or segment - otherwise this should probably leave the theme.

VOLTAS.rationale: Reports on 14 August into the same conditions that just cut Blue Star's room-AC EBIT margin from 5.8% to 2.9%. Voltas is more RAC-weighted than Blue Star and has disclosed no offsetting data-centre business, so the read-across is unfavourable and lands within days.
VOLTAS.watch: A Q1 print showing pricing held better than Blue Star's would invalidate the read-across.
